A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PrivacyRestore and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Inspection of all 22 pages of v3 and 35 pages of v5 supports comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: V3 reports original utility, throughput, privacy-attack, and ablation results on three medical/legal datasets in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: V5 retains original empirical results and adds experiments on output leakage, additional attacks, anonymization baselines, unseen privacy types, sanitization, and excessive span removal.

M1.justification: V5 introduces BERT/MLP classification of varied user-marked spans into predefined privacy types and an optional BERT/Qwen sanitization pipeline when users cannot identify spans (Appendices G and T). It also adopts sampling-based generation for output protection. The shared edited-head selection, ORPO restoration training, and attention-aware aggregation remain.

E1.justification: The same three medical/legal datasets remain, but evaluated scenarios expand substantially. V5 tests privacy types outside the predefined set, users unable to identify spans, excessive removal of nonprivate text, and leakage through outputs and internal representations (Section 6.6; Appendices P, Q, S, T, and X).

E2.justification: V5 adds No Restoration and No Protection to the main utility comparison; No Protection previously appeared as an attack reference. Appendix N/Table 7 adds evaluated LLM-anonymization and IncogniText baselines, and Table 14 includes sanitization-only comparisons. The original three privacy-preserving comparators remain.

E3.justification: Reported service generation changes from greedy decoding with 256 tokens to sampling at temperature 1.0 with 1024 tokens. GPT-4 replaces GPT-3.5 for judging and privacy labeling, and dataset construction adds query rewriting. Privacy calibration changes from average quantities to maxima and a stated common budget of 150; attack inputs and encoders also change. These reported revisions do not establish that the retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: V5 adds output-temperature/leakage analysis, contextual and simulated-steering attacks, hidden-state attacks, restricted privacy-type coverage, automatic sanitization, excessive-removal robustness, and privacy-type frequency analysis. The existing aggregation ablation, edited-head sweep, and Llama-13B study are retained under new numbering. V3's calibration-distribution plots are removed.

E5.justification: Both Table 1 captions specify three runs with averages and variances. V5 Table 12 extends the same three-experiment variance-reporting convention to a new identification experiment. No changed run-count policy, seed disclosure, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: All twelve original Table 1 mean/variance rows are retained exactly, as are the aggregation and edited-head ablation values. V5 nevertheless adds substantial results: Pri-DDXPlus No Protection and No Restoration MC1 scores are 64.88 and 33.57, while PrivacyRestore remains 62.97; automatic sanitization plus restoration reports 62.87 (Table 14). Additional attack, baseline, robustness, and resource results substantially expand the evidence.

T1.justification: V3's formal CDP/LDP definitions and theorem asserting linear budget growth across DP variants are removed. V5 extends the retained meta-vector derivation from epsilon times vector distance to an explicit 2-epsilon bound using normalization (Theorem 5.1, Appendix H). Appendix I adds a softmax/exponential-mechanism derivation with budget 2 times logit sensitivity divided by temperature.

C1.justification: The central restoration contribution remains, but v5 narrows the claimed solution to linear budget growth from DP variants generally to word-level privatization and adds explicit output-protection claims through sampling. The introduction also replaces the finite-span premise with a long-tailed privacy-type premise, changing the advertised applicability beyond an exhaustively predefined span inventory.

C2.justification: V5 adds explanations for handling unseen types, combining restoration with sanitization, and why server-specific restoration vectors impede simulated-steering attacks. It interprets the new controls and resource measurements as supporting practical deployment. New Limitations and Ethics sections acknowledge restricted domain coverage, incomplete attack coverage, and possible biases from the employed LLMs.

D1.justification: V5 adds a stated code/dataset release link, client classifier architecture, query-rewriting prompts, additional attack-training details, and BERT/Qwen sanitization training settings. Appendix V/Table 16 newly reports training times of 7–10 hours and trainable parameter counts. The original five-epoch, batch-size-one restoration training remains documented.

R1.justification: The main SMPC/DP positioning and much of its discussion are retained, with detailed related work moved to Appendix B. Targeted additions discuss LLM-anonymization, IncogniText, complementary text sanitization, informational self-determination, and the exponential mechanism. V3's explicit first-use claim for activation steering in privacy restoration is omitted.

P1.justification: The introduction, threat model, methodology, and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting and reorganization. Detailed related work, training equations, probing, and metric explanations move into reorganized appendices. An appendix overview, limitations, ethics, and acknowledgments are added, and terminology more consistently distinguishes privacy spans from their types.

P2.justification: V5 redraws Figure 1, expands Table 1, adds numerous experimental tables and training, rewriting, and frequency-distribution figures, and removes v3 Figure 4's calibration histograms. Figure 2's epsilon labels and dataset caption change, while the relocated Llama-13B plot gains numerical labels. Tables, figures, and body text are extensively reformatted and reflowed.

improvement.justification: V5 addresses important omissions with utility controls, broader attack tests, practical extensions, reproducibility information, and an explicit meta-vector bound. However, unchanged main-table results accompany revised decoding, judging, and privacy settings without reconciliation. Its new budget calibration also contains material inconsistencies: Table 6's Pri-SLJA paraphrase settings imply 2×193/0.78 ≈ 495 under Appendix M's formula, versus the stated common budget of 150. These problems leave the reliability of central comparisons, and therefore the net quality improvement, uncertain.
